channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
item.description: Parkinson sat out on Wednesday and Thursday. His Friday participation level has not yet been released, but he is probably on the wrong side of questionable at this time. Parkinson does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues, especially with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) expected to play.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Jordan Whittington (back) is questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.
item.description: Whittington has just two catches on the season, and with head coach Sean McVay suggesting he wants to get Tutu Atwell more involved, it seems unlikely Whittington will have a role as more than a returner even if he can play against Washington come Sunday. Trent McDuffie (back) is also questionable for that contest, and won’t practice Friday.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Kelvin Banks (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Browns.
item.description: Banks, the Saints’ talented left tackle, has a chance to return from injured reserve this week. He underwent surgery earlier this year to address a high-ankle sprain. Banks’ backup, Asim Richards (thum), is also questionable to play. Hopefully, at least one of them is good to go.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters that Terrance Ferguson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
item.description: Ferguson will be able to play for the first time since he suffered his medial ankle sprain in Week 3. The second-year tight end offers some volatility, but there’s no denying that there’s upside in his profile. Just don’t be shocked if it isn’t on full display just yet in Week 9.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters Friday that Myles Garrett (knee) is expected to play against the Commanders in Week 9.
item.description: Garrett will need to come off injured reserve, with the Rams likely making that transaction closer to gametime. The 30-year-old has been as good as any defensive player in football, and for the first time he’ll get to be on the same field as Aaron Donald as teammates. Best of luck, Commanders’ offensive line.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Browns.
item.description: We do not yet know Tyson’s participation level at Friday’s practice, but he remained limited on Wednesday and Thursday. It seems like he may need another week before he makes his NFL debut, but we don’t know for sure. If active, Tyson would be FLEX-viable. It is possible the team initially keeps him on a snap count.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Browns.
item.description: Donaldson wasn’t able to practice again Friday, and the 22-year-old tailback won’t be available for the Week 9 skirmish against Cleveland. Alvin Kamara will likely be the top option — and would have been even if Donaldson could play — in that contest, assuming his back injury allows him to play, of course. This is not a great situation, folks.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Harold Fannin was removed from the injury report Friday prior to Week 9 against the Saints.
item.description: Fanning popped up on the report with a groin injury, and there was some added concern because that’s the injury that slowed him during his rookie campaign. The removal brings a sigh of relief for fantasy managers, and Fannin could be in for a big day — at least in terms of targets — with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback for Sunday against New Orleans.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Deshaun Watson (concussion) will not start in Week 9 against the Saints.
item.description: Head coach Todd Monken said Watson will be questionable for Sunday’s game, but has already said Shedeur Sanders will make his first start of the season. Watson missed Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday, although he has yet to clear concussion protocol. The decision to start Sanders likely stems from him working with the first-team offense during the week and the unlikelihood of Watson clearing protocol in time for Sunday’s game.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Shedeur Sanders will start in Week 9 against the Saints.
item.description: Sanders will draw the start as Deshaun Watson (concussion) has yet to clear protocol in time to be ready for Sunday’s game. Interestingly, Watson is still expected to be listed as questionable, per Monken, but Sanders will draw the start. We are assuming this decision is based on Sanders taking first-team reps after Watson missed each of the first two days of practice, but this is a nice opportunity for Sanders to show whatever growth he has made since a tough rookie season in which he threw for 1,440 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions in eight games played. He’ll be on the low-end QB2 radar on the road against the Saints, who rank 16th in fantasy points allowed to opposing QBs this season.-Zachary Krueger
